newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Soft bonds weigh on Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Soft bonds weigh on Australian stocks at open.

text.p: The Australian share market was marginally softer at the open on Monday as bond market concerns over U.S. inflation more than counteracted upbeat signals from a record-breaking Dow.
From the open, the All Ordinaries index lost 0.7 points to 2,417.9.
Brokers said the broader market was drifting as bond yields rose in response to stronger than expected employment data in the U.S. on Friday.
"Bonds here and in the U.S. were off and that has seen us just drift this morning," said a Sydney broker.
While continued weakness on the Japanese stock market was not being totally ignored, the broker said any local impact would be indirect.
"It would be indirect if anything, not like the way the Dow can move things. We have had no real comment here," he said.

Sydney Harbour Casino featured early, its shares soaring over 16 percent to A$2.25 (US$1.76), after Australia's richest man, Kerry Packer, said his Publishing and Broadcasting would buy a 10 percent stake in the casino and the management rights from U.S.-based Showboat Inc.
In the miners, CRA slipped one percent to A$19.38 after its dual-listed partner RTZ lost ground in London.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about three to two, while about 44 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
